title: Hybrid-batch KV footprint characterization and model-specific memory knobs for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Sasha Patel
description: Characterize the KV-cache working-set and GPU memory footprint when serving long-context workloads with our continuous batching runtime. Produce model-specific memory knobs (eviction thresholds, slice sizes, prefault budgets) for Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants to minimize OOMs and tail-latency spikes while preserving throughput.
background: Recent incidents during the 64k and 128k load tests showed burst OOMs when mixed-length requests cause KV residency to exceed expected working sets. Existing heuristics use a one-size-fits-all eviction curve which is suboptimal for models with different KV growth characteristics (sparse attention variants and per-token cache size differences across qwen-14b, mistral-7b, and llama-70b). This ticket consolidates profiling, offline memory-model fitting, and runtime knob rollout.
proposal: 1) Build per-model working-set signatures by sampling real request length distributions and tracking per-token KV bytes, shard residency, and slab fragmentation across batch shapes. 2) Fit a small parametric model (piecewise linear KV-growth curve) per variant and per quantization mode. 3) Derive three runtime knobs: eviction_threshold_pct, kv_slice_target_bytes, and prefault_margin_tokens. 4) Implement a safe canary rollout where Dedicated nodes use the new knobs behind a feature flag and console exposes diagnostics.
experiment_plan: - Phase A (profiling): run long-context synthetic replay and 2 production shadow windows (48h) for each variant (llama-70b-causal, mistral-7b-instruct, qwen-14b) capturing KV residency heatmaps, slab allocation churn, and per-GPU free headroom. - Phase B (fitting): fit per-variant growth curves, validate by predicting OOM points on held-out traces. - Phase C (runtime): enable knobs on 10% of dedicated capacity with rollback if p99 latency > 1.2x baseline or any OOMs occur. - Phase D (scale): propagate knobs and add console recommendations in Optimize.
acceptance_criteria: Per-variant memory profile artifact exists for at least the three target models (artifact links in links field).
End-to-end test: no increase in OOM incidents in the canary pool compared to baseline over 72h
Throughput: token/sec for the canary pool remains within -8%/+3% of baseline under identical load shapes
Tail latency: p99 generation latency stays <= 1.2x baseline for mixed-length workload
Memory headroom improvement: average peak GPU reserved headroom reduced by >= 12% for long-context traces
risks: Risk of over-aggressive eviction causing visible quality degradation (stale KV leading to stale completions) for conversation flows that rely on prefix context. There's also risk of model-to-model variability where a single curve family cannot capture extreme outliers; mitigation is canary rollback and conservative prefault margins.
